title: Boss: on-call in vim
summary: Pull together vimrc, macros and server editing into tools you would really use.

steps.title: Your on-call kit
steps.body: Three pieces of tooling for the day you only have ssh and vim: a write-permission advisor, a macro runner that edits real lines, and an effective-settings report.

steps.title: Can :w work?
prompt: Write `string WritePlan(string owner, string mode, string user, bool userHasSudo, bool isNeovim)` advising what to do when saving a file. `mode` is a symbolic mode like `rw-r--r--` (owner, group, others; ignore groups: treat the user as either the owner or "others").
- if the user can write the file (owner with `w` in the first triplet, or anyone with `w` in the last triplet) → `":w"`
- otherwise, if the user has sudo: `":w !sudo tee % > /dev/null"` in vim, but in neovim `":w /tmp/copy then sudo cp"`
starter: string WritePlan(string owner, string mode, string user, bool userHasSudo, bool isNeovim)
solution: string WritePlan(string owner, string mode, string user, bool userHasSudo, bool isNeovim)
if (userHasSudo) return isNeovim ? ":w /tmp/copy then sudo cp" : ":w !sudo tee % > /dev/null";
hints: The owner's write bit is `mode[1]`, others' is `mode[7]`.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("own file", ":w", WritePlan("ana", "rw-r--r--", "ana", false, false));
Dojo.Eq("root file with sudo in vim", ":w !sudo tee % > /dev/null", WritePlan("root", "rw-r--r--", "ana", true, false));
Dojo.Eq("root file with sudo in neovim", ":w /tmp/copy then sudo cp", WritePlan("root", "rw-r--r--", "ana", true, true));
Dojo.Eq("world-writable", ":w", WritePlan("root", "rw-rw-rw-", "ana", false, false));
Dojo.Eq("read-only even for the owner", "ask an admin", WritePlan("ana", "r--r--r--", "ana", false, false));
Dojo.Eq("no sudo", "ask an admin", WritePlan("root", "rw-r--r--", "ana", false, false));

steps.title: Run a macro over lines
prompt: Write `List<string> RunMacro(List<string> lines, string macro, int times)` that runs a macro on the buffer, starting with the cursor at line 0, column 0. The macro uses only these keys:
- `0` start of line, `$` last character, `j` down a line (if there is no next line, **the macro stops** and so do all remaining repetitions, just like vim),
- `I` / `A` + text + `\u001b`: insert at the start / append at the end,
- `x` delete the character under the cursor,
- `dd` delete the line (the cursor stays at the same index, clamped).
Run the whole macro `times` times. Return the lines.
starter: List<string> RunMacro(List<string> lines, string macro, int times)
solution: List<string> RunMacro(List<string> lines, string macro, int times)
else if (k == '$') { col = Math.Max(0, text[row].Length - 1); i++; }
row++; col = Math.Min(col, Math.Max(0, text[row].Length - 1)); i++;
if (k == 'I') { text[row] = typed + text[row]; col = Math.Max(0, typed.Length - 1); }
else { text[row] = text[row] + typed; col = Math.Max(0, text[row].Length - 1); }
if (text[row].Length > 0) { text[row] = text[row].Remove(col, 1); col = Math.Min(col, Math.Max(0, text[row].Length - 1)); }
hints: Walk the macro with an index `i`; `I` and `A` consume everything up to the next Esc.
A `j` on the last line ends the whole run: `return`.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("append ; and move down, 3 times", new List<string> { "a;", "b;", "c;", "d" }, RunMacro(new List<string> { "a", "b", "c", "d" }, "A;\u001bj", 3));
Dojo.Eq("stops at the end of the file", new List<string> { "- a", "- b" }, RunMacro(new List<string> { "a", "b" }, "0I- \u001bj", 100));
Dojo.Eq("uncomment with 0xj", new List<string> { "port=80", "host=x" }, RunMacro(new List<string> { "#port=80", "#host=x" }, "0xj", 5));
Dojo.Eq("delete every line", new List<string>(), RunMacro(new List<string> { "a", "b", "c" }, "dd", 10));
Dojo.Eq("quote every line", new List<string> { "\"a\",", "\"b\"," }, RunMacro(new List<string> { "a", "b" }, "0I\"\u001bA\",\u001bj", 2));

steps.title: Effective settings report
prompt: Write `List<string> Report(string[] systemVimrc, string[] userVimrc, string[] modeline)` that applies three sources in order (later wins) and returns `"<name>=<value> (<source>)"` lines sorted by name (ordinal), where source is `system`, `user` or `modeline`, the **last** source that set that option.
- The two vimrc arrays use the `set` syntax from lesson 1 (`name`, `noname`, `name=value`, `name!`; comments with `"`).

- `modeline` is one line like `# vim: set ts=2 sw=2 et:`; the options are between `set ` and the final `:`. Abbreviations map: `ts`→`tabstop`, `sw`→`shiftwidth`, `et`→`expandtab`, `noet`→`noexpandtab`, `nu`→`number`.
starter: List<string> Report(string[] systemVimrc, string[] userVimrc, string[] modeline)
solution: List<string> Report(string[] systemVimrc, string[] userVimrc, string[] modeline)
string Full(string n) => abbrev.TryGetValue(n, out var f) ? f : n;
if (eq > 0) { name = Full(item.Substring(0, eq)); values[name] = item.Substring(eq + 1); }
else if (item.EndsWith("!")) { name = Full(item.TrimEnd('!')); values[name] = values.TryGetValue(name, out var v) && v == "true" ? "false" : "true"; }
foreach (var item in line.Substring(4).Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries)) Apply(item, src);
foreach (var item in m.Substring(s + 4, e - s - 4).Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries)) Apply(item, "modeline");
hints: Write one `Apply(item, source)` that updates both a value and a source dictionary.
For the modeline, take the text between `set ` and the last `:`.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoSys = new[] { "set nocompatible", "set tabstop=8", "set hlsearch" };
var dojoUser = new[] { "\" mine", "set expandtab shiftwidth=4 tabstop=4", "set nohlsearch" };
var dojoMode = new[] { "# vim: set ts=2 sw=2 noet:" };
Dojo.Eq("all three sources", new List<string> {
"compatible=false (system)",
"expandtab=false (modeline)",
"hlsearch=false (user)",
"shiftwidth=2 (modeline)",
"tabstop=2 (modeline)" }, Report(dojoSys, dojoUser, dojoMode));
Dojo.Eq("no modeline", new List<string> { "number=true (user)" }, Report(new string[0], new[] { "set nu" }, new string[0]));
Dojo.Eq("toggle across files", new List<string> { "number=false (user)" }, Report(new[] { "set number" }, new[] { "set number!" }, new string[0]));
